subject: Post-call recap: on-prem / VPC discovery — residency, air-gap, next steps
messages:
From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
To: John Patel <john.patel@medsafehealth.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 30 May 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap: on-prem / VPC discovery — residency, air-gap, next steps

John — thanks again for taking time today. Below is a concise recap of what we heard, the main constraints driving this evaluation, and proposed next steps. Please let us know if anything below is off.

Key pain points & drivers
- Data residency/regulatory: patient records must remain in-state (CA) and cannot traverse third-party regions. Auditability (KMS/HSM logs) is mandatory.
- Air-gap considerations: primary environment is effectively air-gapped for model inference; outbound connections are restricted to approved endpoints and must use a proxy jump.
- Procurement/timeline: target pilot with 1-2 models in Q3; procurement needs an EULA + network diagram to start legal review.

Technical constraints (what we heard)
- No direct internet egress from the compute VPC except to a small allowlist (IP ranges + signed cert pinning).
- Strict firewall: only TLS 443 outbound to pre-authorized IPs; no outbound DNS resolution to public names unless via internal resolver.
- Separate management plane: they want Redwood control plane traffic routed through a customer-managed VPN to meet audit requirements.

Goals & success criteria
- Latency target: 250–400ms p95 for inference from on-prem app to private inference endpoints.
- Cost target: predictable committed capacity for pilot month-to-month with ability to scale.
- Security: SOC2 evidence, KMS-integrated key management, and on-prem log forwarding for audit retention.

Proposed next steps (owner — due)
- Rachel: share a networking matrix template and a short checklist for on-prem prep — attached (networking-matrix-template.xlsx). — Due: Tue 6/1
- John / Infra: confirm list of allowed egress IPs and whether a customer proxy/jump-host is required — Due: Fri 6/3
- Ben: prepare initial commercial draft (pilot pricing + reserved capacity options) and hand to Procurement (Maria) — Due: Mon 6/6
- Neha: schedule a technical deep-dive with A. Singh (infra) + their security lead (30–45m) — Proposed window: week of 6/6

Attachments referenced
- networking-matrix-template.xlsx (attachment)
- medsafe-security-questionnaire_v2.pdf (they asked for an updated version; attached)

Thanks again — we’ll keep this lightweight and prioritize the infra deep-dive so we can validate the egress + proxy pattern.

— Rachel Kim
Enterprise Solutions | Redwood Inference
rachel.kim@redwood.com | (415) 555-0142
From: John Patel <john.patel@medsafehealth.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
Cc: Maria Gomez <maria.gomez@medsafehealth.com>, A. Singh <asingh@medsafehealth.com>
Date: Sun, 30 May 2027 16:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: on-prem / VPC discovery — residency, air-gap, next steps

Rachel — this is great, thank you. Confirming a few clarifications: 
1) We do need the management/control plane traffic to go over our VPN; we cannot expose management ports directly to the public internet.
2) For allowed egress, we can provide specific IP ranges; names/pins are preferred but our infra requires IP allowlisting at the firewall layer.
3) I’ve looped in Maria (Procurement) to start the paperwork once Ben shares the pilot commercial.

We’ll get the IP list and a rough network diagram by Tue 6/1. Also, can your team confirm whether Redwood agents can run entirely inside our VPC (no outbound at all) if we provide a managed NAT/proxy? That is the blocker for our security team.

Thanks — John
Director, IT Infrastructure | MedSafe Health
john.patel@medsafehealth.com | +1 415-777-8900

- Agent-in-VPC: yes — with a customer-managed NAT/proxy we can avoid direct internet egress. We’ll validate required outbound endpoints in the tech deep-dive (Priyom to own).
